major_concerns: Emulator fidelity vs production (external validity) may limit claim scope.
Dual-use / disclosure risk from published failing configs.
Definition and operationalization of 'semantic/functional failure' needs tighter, pre-registered specification.
Budget and API-rate exposure for 2,000 model calls needs explicit guardrails.
required_design_repairs: Specify emulator fidelity targets and justify topology choices; document limits to external validity in preregistration.
Redact sensitive topology/device details and define safe-publication policy for failure examples.
Provide an explicit, machine-readable failure taxonomy with deterministic detection rules and thresholds.
Add concrete budget/stop rules tied to model-call limits and cost caps; confirm hosted-model availability and exact model identifier(s).
Predefine randomization/seeding, exclusion rules, and logging/hash manifest formats.

major_concerns: Risk that repairs overfit to validator blind spots (false sense of safety).
Potential for GVR to introduce new, unvalidated failure modes.
Need to ensure paired design preserves independence assumptions for McNemar test.
Cost and rate limits from up to 3 repair iterations per task.
required_design_repairs: Include validator-coverage diagnostics and a secondary independent validator or randomized holdout checks to detect overfitting to validator rules.
Predefine detection and logging for newly introduced failure types and criteria for treating GVR as harmful.
Clarify statistical assumptions, plan for dependency handling, and register exact McNemar implementation and multiple-comparison corrections.
Preregister repair-prompt templates, iteration stopping rules, and maximum per-task call budget; include runtime budget enforcement.

major_concerns: High dual-use / ethical risk from publishing adversarial templates and exploit traces.
Emulator success may not map to production exploitability (external validity).
Reproducibility challenges if adversarial templates are redacted or if hosted models change behavior.
Need for oversight/ethics clearance and a responsible-disclosure plan.
required_design_repairs: Obtain and document an institutional ethical review or equivalent risk assessment; include a redaction and responsible-disclosure plan in preregistration.
Limit public release of adversarial templates; publish abstracted findings and sanitized representative traces only.
Include baseline controls and validation that emulator-detected unsafe changes correspond to meaningful operational harms; state limits of transferability to production.
Preregister exact adversarial-template generation process, stopping rules, and safety constraints; define how reproducible artifacts will be provided without enabling misuse.

major_concerns: Large-factor design depends on stable access to multiple hosted-model families (availability risk).
Simulated context-window truncation (dropping oldest context) may not faithfully emulate shorter-window model behavior—threat to construct validity.
High multiple-comparisons burden and analytic complexity; requires clear preregistered analysis pipeline.
Resource/cost risk for ~9,720 cases if substitutes or retries are needed.
required_design_repairs: Preregister exact model identifiers and acceptable substitution hierarchy; include contingency plan if a model becomes unavailable.
Justify and document the context-truncation method and validate it with a small pilot showing it approximates true short-context behavior where possible.
Provide a detailed, preregistered mixed-effects analysis plan, correction methods for multiple testing, and power/sample-size justification.
Add budget caps, sampling/reduction strategy if cost limits hit (e.g., stratified subsampling), and exact logging/seeding procedures.
